parts.gloss: those who abandoned their own relations

words.gloss: those who abandoned their own relations

literal: Those who were relations and abandoned their own, their kinship, when the reason for dislike is without, will return.
translation: Those who were once relations and abandoned their family will return to that kinship of their own accord when the cause of their dislike is gone.
modern: உறவினர்களாக இருந்து பிரிந்து சென்றவர்கள், தங்களுக்குள் இருந்த வெறுப்புக்கான காரணம் நீங்கியவுடன், மீண்டும் உறவினர்களாகத் தேடி வருவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet describes how estranged relatives can be reunited. It explains that when those who were once close kinsmen (தமராகி) abandon their family (தற்றுறந்தார்), they will return (வரும்) to the fold of kinship (சுற்றம்). This reunion happens naturally once the underlying cause (காரணம்) for their dislike or lack of harmony (அமராமை) is removed or ceases to exist (இன்றி). The poet emphasizes that relationships are resilient, and once misunderstandings are cleared, unity is restored.
